title: Two Engineers Argue About Whether They Made Anything Beautiful
script: Galih: [uneasy] Six years building this recommendation engine, and I've started wondering whether we've built anything I'd actually defend on its merits, or merely something that works.
Prita: [pointed] Those aren't mutually exclusive, Galih. Plenty of things work brilliantly while being, in some larger sense, indefensible.
Galih: [candid] That's rather my worry, precisely. It optimizes for engagement with a ruthlessness I find difficult to admire, even as I remain professionally proud of the elegance underneath it.

Prita: [thoughtful] I've made peace with that particular tension, mostly by separating the craft from the deployment. The engineering can be beautiful even when its application is, at minimum, ethically ambiguous.
Galih: [challenging] Can it, though? Or is that distinction just a convenient partition we've built to protect our own conscience from the thing we're actually paid to optimize?

Prita: [conceding] Possibly. I won't pretend the partition is airtight. But the alternative, refusing any craft whose downstream use might be questionable, would rule out nearly every consequential piece of engineering ever built.
Galih: [considering] Fair, and yet there's a meaningful difference between unpredictable downstream misuse and an outcome we deliberately engineered toward from the outset.

Prita: [firm] Agreed, and that distinction is exactly where I think our actual responsibility sits, not in refusing the work, but in refusing to look away from what we've deliberately optimized it to do.
Galih: [honest] I haven't been looking away, if I'm honest. I've been looking directly at it and simply telling myself the elegance excuses the target.
Prita: [gently] That's a harder confession than most engineers manage. Most of us prefer the comfortable fiction that neutrality is even available to us.
Galih: [resolved] I don't think it is, not anymore. I think I'd rather build something less impressive that I could actually stand behind without flinching.
Prita: [warmly] Then propose it. I'd rather argue with you about a worse metric and a clearer conscience than keep perfecting a machine neither of us can fully defend.

quiz.question: What has Galih started wondering after six years on the recommendation engine?
options: Whether it works technically
Whether they've built anything he'd actually defend on its merits, beyond it simply working
Whether to quit engineering entirely
Whether Prita is a good colleague
quiz.explanation: Galih wonders whether they've built something defensible on its merits, not merely something functional.

quiz.question: How does Prita initially try to reconcile the tension Galih raises?
options: By ignoring the problem entirely
By separating the craft from the deployment, seeing engineering as beautiful even when its application is ambiguous
By quitting the project immediately
By blaming users for misuse
quiz.explanation: Prita separates the elegance of the craft from the ethics of its deployment as her initial coping strategy.

quiz.question: What distinction does Galih draw regarding downstream effects?
options: There is no meaningful distinction to draw
A difference between unpredictable misuse and an outcome deliberately engineered toward from the outset
All outcomes are equally the engineers' fault
Only regulators can determine responsibility
quiz.explanation: Galih distinguishes between unpredictable downstream misuse and a deliberately engineered outcome.

quiz.question: What confession does Galih make about his own behavior?
options: That he has been ignoring the ethical questions entirely
That he has been looking directly at the issue and telling himself the elegance excuses the target
That he never noticed any ethical tension
That he wants to blame Prita
quiz.explanation: Galih admits he has been looking directly at the problem while telling himself elegance excuses the target.

quiz.question: What does Galih ultimately decide he would rather build?
options: Nothing at all, leaving the field
Something less impressive that he could actually stand behind without flinching
An even more engagement-optimized system
A system identical to the current one
quiz.explanation: Galih resolves he would rather build something less impressive that he could stand behind without flinching.
